chunks: Rasul-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said:

The example of the believer is like the tender shoot of a crop: the winds bend it this way and that; likewise, the believer is bent by pains and illnesses. And the example of the hypocrite is like a straight iron bar which nothing affects until death comes to it and breaks it utterly.

key_terms.الرِّيَاحُ: the winds, symbolizing the forces that strike and sway a person
key_terms.الْأَمْرَاضُ: illnesses, afflictions that befall the believer
key_terms.الْأَوْجَاعُ: pains, referring to bodily suffering and hardship
key_terms.الْمَوْتُ: death, which comes decisively in the end
key_terms.الْمُؤْمِنِ: the believer, whose condition is marked by receptiveness to worldly afflictions
key_terms.الْمُنَافِقِ: the hypocrite, outwardly firm but inwardly lacking true faith
key_terms.خَامَةِ الزَّرْعِ: the tender shoot of a crop, used as a simile for delicacy and flexibility
key_terms.قَصْفًا: a breaking utterly, indicating severe and sudden destruction

ai.seo_question: How does the hadith compare the believer and the hypocrite in facing afflictions?
ai.summary: This hadith likens the believer to a tender plant that bends under the force of winds, just as the believer is afflicted by pains and illnesses in this world. It contrasts this with the hypocrite, who appears firm and untouched until death suddenly strikes and destroys him.
